clue.text: Fear Ruby will suffer in period of atonement

indicators.note: something that suffers is knocked about, so the words 'Fear' and 'Ruby' get knocked out of shape

parts.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: A woman called Ruby is warned that fear will torment her through some solemn season of penance.
explanation.walkthrough: The month takes its name from the Roman februa, rites of purification held in it, which is why Rufus can call FEBRUARY a period of atonement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin root means purification, so the Roman calendar treated this month as the season for cleansing and expiation rituals.

clue.text: Point to a hundred in stock that's prolific

indicators.note: the point and the hundred sit in 'stock', so the stock word wraps round them

parts.note: a stock or reserve of money
a compass point: east
the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A farmer points to a hundred head in a herd that breeds well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' tempts you towards farm animals, which suits 'prolific', but here it is a store of money. E and C join first, then go inside FUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something highly fertile, producing offspring or ideas in great abundance; they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Piece of the cloth?

definitions.meaning: a man of the cloth is a clergyman, the cloth being the clergy's dress

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, 'Piece of the cloth' is a scrap of fabric; split it, and a chess piece meets a churchman. 'The cloth' is an old phrase for the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess piece shares its name with a senior clergyman, and clergy collectively are called the cloth, so both halves fit.

clue.text: All agreed to distribution of a union sum

indicators.note: a distribution spreads things out afresh, so the letters of 'a union sum' are dealt out in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: Members of a trade union all vote in favour of how a sum of money is to be shared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distribution' fits the surface of shares being handed out, which hides that it is the instruction to rearrange 'a union sum'.
explanation.definitionFit: When a vote is carried with every single member in favour and nobody dissenting, the decision is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Turbulent masses resent another valuation

indicators.note: turbulent means churned up, so 'masses resent' is stirred into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, twelve letters

explanation.surface: An angry crowd objects to a fresh property valuation, perhaps for a new tax.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is exact to the letter: 'masses resent' holds the four Ss and three Es the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to put a value on something, so doing it again gives a second or revised estimate of worth.

clue.text: Score a number

definitions.meaning: a score is an old counting noun for a set, as in 'three score years and ten'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like a verb about goals or points, but it is the old counting noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a traditional unit meaning a set of that many, as in 'three score years and ten'; the second half is plain.

clue.text: Strange device to raise river level before dam opens

indicators.note: the device comes before the dam in the answer, so the two pieces sit in that order

parts.note: a low dam built across a river to hold the water back

indicators.note: what opens a word is its first letter, so only the start of 'dam' is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of 'dam'

explanation.surface: An engineer describes an odd contraption that lifts a river before the dam's sluices open.
explanation.walkthrough: A weir is itself a sort of dam, so the clue plays both sides: the long phrase is the WEIR, and 'dam' only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something odd, uncanny or out of the ordinary; they are simple synonyms.

clue.text: Painkiller used on Arctic trip

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so 'on Arctic' tumbles into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: An explorer takes painkillers along on a polar expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' reads as a journey and doubles as slang for a drug experience, which suits the answer; its job here is to stir the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates such as morphine relieve pain and dull the senses, so a drug of this class is a painkiller.

clue.text: Desire of head changing study

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and here the first letter of 'study' is swapped for another

parts.note: study, as in book learning; its first letter is the one that changes

explanation.surface: A student longs to change the subject of their studies.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the L at the front of LEARNING for a Y and you get YEARNING; the clue leaves you to find the new letter from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep longing or strong wish for something is a desire, so the noun and the definition are synonyms.

clue.text: Unfortunate craftsman left to fend for himself

definitions.text: Unfortunate craftsman left to fend for himself

parts.note: surface reading: an unlucky artisan, a carpenter or potter out of work

parts.words: craftsman left to fend for himself
parts.note: setter's reading: a man from a craft, a boat, who is shipwrecked and marooned alone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Craftsman' splits as craft's man: a craft is a vessel, so this is a sailor from a wrecked ship stranded on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipwrecked sailor abandoned on a desert island must survive alone, which is exactly the plight the clue describes.

clue.text: Code word for "S" is rare in operation

indicators.note: something in operation is being worked on, so 'is rare' is worked into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, six letters

explanation.surface: A radio operator remarks that one letter's call sign is seldom used on a military mission.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks round the S make the definition look like wordplay; it is the definition itself, asking for a radio code word.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet used by pilots and radio operators, each letter has a spoken name, and this is the one for S.

clue.text: Northern tourist attraction needs law on handrails reinstated

indicators.note: something reinstated is put back up after being taken down, so 'law' and 'handrails' are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: part of the anagram fodder
the rest of the fodder; 'on' just sets it beside 'law'

explanation.surface: A popular site in the north of England needs rules about its safety railings put back in force.
explanation.walkthrough: HADRIAN'S WALL is the Roman wall across northern England, from Tyne to Solway, now a heritage trail. 'On' only places the two words side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Roman frontier across northern England draws many visitors to its forts and footpaths, making it a famous sightseeing destination.

clue.text: Ruth's mother-in-law caused no end of a minor riot

indicators.note: with no end, the word 'minor' loses its final letter
a riot is disorder, so the shortened words are thrown into a new order

parts.note: used as it stands
'minor' with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A biblical matriarch is blamed for starting a small disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Ruth, the widowed Ruth stays loyal to her husband's mother, NAOMI, and follows her to Bethlehem.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament story tells how the Moabite widow refused to leave her late husband's mother, who bore this name.

clue.text: Leave the witness box and go off duty

definitions.meaning: what a judge tells a witness who has finished giving evidence
what troops or guards do when relieved from their posts

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are fixed phrases: a witness is told to step down from the box, and soldiers are released from readiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtroom witness is dismissed with this phrase, and military units relieved of readiness are said to do the same thing.

clue.text: Conversation is about management of natural resources

indicators.note: 'about' means turned around, so the letters of 'Conversation' are turned into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, twelve letters

explanation.surface: Someone reports what a discussion was about: looking after the planet's resources.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is about' reads as 'concerns', a natural way to describe a talk; here 'about' only stirs the letters, and only V and S swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Protecting forests, wildlife and water by using them carefully and preventing waste is the work environmentalists call by this name.

clue.text: Club menu the AA had changed?

indicators.note: if the words 'menu the AA' had changed, their letters now stand in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A gentleman's club wonders whether a motoring organisation has altered its dining menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The Athenaeum is a famous London gentlemen's club on Pall Mall; the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring breakdown service.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a well-known private members' institution in London, founded for writers, scientists and artists.

clue.text: Volunteers get increasing presents

parts.note: to volunteer something is to offer it
prices that are increasing are up

explanation.surface: Volunteers are given more and more gifts for their help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volunteers' and 'presents' both read as nouns in the surface, people and gifts, but each is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something forward for acceptance, as a gift, prayer or sacrifice, is both to present it and to offer it up.

clue.text: Springtime — when women propose to break with tradition

definitions.meaning: read cryptically, not as the season: a time for springing, or jumping

definitions.text: when women propose to break with tradition
definitions.meaning: the year in which, by old custom, a woman may ask a man to marry her

explanation.walkthrough: 'Springtime' reads as the season, but split it: spring is to leap, a time is a year. By old British and Irish folklore, a woman may propose to a man on 29 February.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk custom allows women to make the marriage proposal on the extra day in February, so the whole year with that day is meant.

clue.text: Seems return for my passage will be by end of day — pity!

parts.note: as in 'it feels cold': it seems

indicators.note: to return is to come back, so the word 'my' runs back the other way

parts.note: taken as written, before being turned round
a path is a way through

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only the final letter of 'day' is used

parts.note: the final letter of 'day'

explanation.surface: A traveller grumbles that the homeward trip will only come at day's end, what a shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' and 'passage' conjure a travel ticket; they are really a reversal and a PATH. 'By' simply places the final piece after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel sorrow and compassion for someone's suffering is to pity them, so the phrase and the verb are synonyms.

clue.text: Business expense on company's time

parts.note: used as it stands
CO is the usual short form of company, plus the S of the possessive
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An employee's expenses are incurred during working hours, on the firm's time.
explanation.walkthrough: An ONCOST is a British term for an overhead: a running cost of a business, like rent or heating, not tied to any one product.
explanation.definitionFit: Accountants in Britain use this word for overheads, the general running costs a firm pays beyond direct production costs.

clue.text: Hearing Arab leaders gives us the shivers!

indicators.note: hearing a word means taking it by ear, so 'Arab leaders' counts for its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: sheikhs are Arab chiefs, and many speakers say the title to rhyme with 'makes'

explanation.surface: Someone is frightened just by listening to powerful Arab rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' looks as if it might pick out first letters of 'Arab', but 'Arab leaders' is a whole title, SHEIKHS, taken by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the shakes means trembling from fear, cold or illness, which is also what having the shivers means; both are plural nouns.

clue.text: Could be next Open Champions, perhaps

definitions.text: Could be next Open Champions, perhaps

indicators.note: 'could be' says the letters might become something else, so 'next Open' plus a plural ending are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, eight letters
the plural ending of 'Champions' joins the fodder

explanation.surface: A pundit predicts who might win the next Open golf championship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open is golf's oldest major championship. The whole clue defines, since future champions are exponents of the game; the fodder is one letter short, so the S of 'Champions' is borrowed.
explanation.definitionFit: An exponent is a leading practitioner of a skill, and the golfers who will win the next championship are prime examples of such masters.

clue.text: Recess in pleasant hospital

indicators.note: the hospital goes in 'pleasant', so the pleasant word is split round it

parts.note: a pleasant day is a nice day
H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A quiet alcove in an agreeable hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' could be a break in Parliament's sittings; here it is an alcove in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow hollow set into a wall, often to hold a statue or ornament, is an alcove or recess.

clue.text: Man in the orchestra playing Beethoven's Choral Symphony

indicators.note: the answer is playing inside the words 'Man in the', performing from within them as a member of an orchestra does

parts.note: the letters run across the word boundaries of 'Man in the'
surface padding: it sets the concert scene and gives no letters

explanation.surface: A musician sits in the orchestra performing Beethoven's great choral symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a picture of a concert, so 'Man in the orchestra' reads as a player; the answer is tucked into 'maN IN THe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's final completed symphony, with its sung 'Ode to Joy', is known as the Choral, and carries the number nine.

clue.text: Address for delivery?

definitions.meaning: a formal talk given to an audience, as in the Gettysburg Address
a speaker's manner of talking, as in 'her delivery was halting'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' and 'delivery' both look like postal words, a place for the postman to bring a parcel; each is really about talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal oration is an address, and the way someone talks aloud, their diction and delivery, is also called by this noun.

clue.text: Ready to stand up to trained fighter

parts.note: game for anything: willing, ready
to cock is to make stand up, as a horse cocks its ears

explanation.surface: A boxer is prepared to confront a well-trained opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a boxer squaring up; the fighter is in fact a bird bred for cockfighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel bred and raised specifically for cockfighting contests is a fighting bird, so it is a trained combatant.

clue.text: He may handle your case

parts.note: surface reading: a lawyer who takes on your legal case
setter's reading: someone at a station or hotel who carries your suitcase

explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' points to a lawyer, and 'handle' to managing a matter; both are meant literally, a suitcase lifted by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway stations and hotels employ staff to carry travellers' luggage, and a suitcase is often just called a case.

clue.text: Lime and cats affected plant

indicators.note: things affected have been acted on and altered, so 'lime' and 'cats' come out in a new order

parts.note: part of the anagram fodder
the rest of the fodder; 'and' joins them

explanation.surface: A gardener finds that lime in the soil and neighbourhood cats have damaged a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Lime is a real concern for gardeners, as it alters soil, so the surface is plausible; clematis in fact likes lime.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a climbing garden shrub with large showy flowers, one specific example of the general category of plants.
